newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Lebanon did not issue weekly CDs.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Lebanon did not issue weekly CDs.

text.p: There were no offers for the Bank of Lebanon's weekly issue of certificates of deposit on Thursday, a central bank source said.
The source said investors were instead buying two-year treasury bills at 20.76 percent per annum.
"Everyone is rushing to buy two year T-bills that carry high interest rates," the source told Reuter.
The 45-day and 60-day CDs currently carry interest rates of 12.25 percent and 13 percent.
The Bank said on Monday its latest weekly T-bill issue dated December 5 raised 468.7 billion Lebanese pounds, of which two-year bills totalled 265.4 billion.
Last week the Bank sold 45-day CDs worth two billion pounds and 60-day CDs worth two billion pounds.
It was the third time that the central bank has failed to make a weekly CD issue due to lack of market interest since it introduced the paper in November 1994.
